text: On 28 May 2023 the user said they were thinking of planning a trip abroad soon and asked for travel tips on affordable accommodation and on packing light.

The assistant suggested affordable accommodation options for the user's trip abroad: hostels booked through Hostelworld, Hostelbookers or Booking.com, budget hotels or guesthouses via Booking.com, Agoda or Expedia, Airbnb rentals, Couchsurfing stays, and house-sitting through TrustedHousesitters or HouseCarers.

The assistant's packing-light advice was to pack only essentials, choose multi-purpose items such as a sarong that doubles as a blanket, towel or dress, roll clothes instead of folding them, and pack a portable laundry kit with travel detergent, a travel washline and clothespins.
On 28 May 2023 the user said they had been trying out new recipes lately and had already tried 3 of Emma's recipes, which they found all amazing.
On 28 May 2023 the user said they were thinking of visiting Europe, maybe Spain or Italy, and asked for country-specific tips plus recommendations for vegan restaurants in those areas.

The assistant recommended vegan restaurants in Spain and Italy. Spain: Vega Life in Barcelona (fully vegan, international dishes), Green & Vibrant in Madrid (plant-based, gluten-free, refined sugar-free) and VEGGI in Seville (100% vegan). Italy: Flower Burger in Milan (vegan burgers), Joia in Rome (a Michelin-starred vegan restaurant) and Vegan Glory in Florence (vegan and gluten-free options, including vegan gelato).
The assistant said Italy's truffle season runs from October to December, and for Spain recommended tapas bars in Barcelona, Madrid and Seville and flamenco shows in Seville, Granada or Madrid.
On 28 May 2023 the user said they were really interested in trying out more vegan restaurants and asked for recommendations on vegan cooking classes or workshops in Spain and Italy.

The assistant recommended vegan cooking classes in Barcelona: Vegan Cooking Barcelona (hands-on Catalan and Spanish cuisine with a vegan twist) and Cookly (including a 'Vegan Tapas' class). For Rome it listed Vegan Cooking Rome and Cookly (including a 'Vegan Italian Feast' class).

The assistant recommended vegan cooking classes in Madrid (Vegan Madrid Cooking School and Escuela de Cocina Vegana) and Florence (Florence Vegan Cooking School and Vegan Italy, including a 'Vegan Tuscan Feast' class), plus vegan cooking retreats such as Vegan Retreat Spain, La Casa Verde and Vegan Retreat Italy.

On 28 May 2023 the user said they would look into the cooking classes in Barcelona and Rome and asked for tips on finding affordable accommodation in central locations, close to the classes and the cities' main sights.

The assistant suggested staying in central Barcelona neighbourhoods El Raval, Gothic Quarter or Eixample, with hostels Hostel One Ramblas, Meetingpoint Hostel and Sun & Moon Hostel, and budget hotels Hotel Europa Style and Hotel Curious. For central Rome it suggested Centro Storico, Trastevere or Monti, with Hostel Colosseum, M&J Place Hostel, Alessandro Palace Hostel near Termini station, and Hotel Des Artistes and Hotel Panda.
On 28 May 2023 the user said they planned to spend around 5-7 days in Barcelona and Rome and asked how to get around while carrying cooking class ingredients and equipment.

The assistant said Barcelona has 12 metro lines and over 100 bus lines, both covered by the Hola BCN card for unlimited public transport, with the Bicing bike-share as an option. For Rome it said there are three metro lines, over 300 bus lines and six tram lines, all covered by the Roma Pass for unlimited travel.
On 28 May 2023 the user said they would take a taxi or ride-hailing service if carrying lots of ingredients and equipment, and asked for must-try vegan dishes in Barcelona and Rome.

The assistant recommended Barcelona vegan specialties: pa amb tomàquet at Vegetalia and Barceloneta's Vegan Beach Bar, escalivada at Teresa Carles Health Food and Green & Vibrant, and churros con chocolate at Churreria La Lola and Bar Oveja Verde.

The assistant recommended Rome vegan specialties: pasta alla carbonara at Il Margutta and Ops! Roma, supplì at Vegan Junk Food Bar and Flower Burger, and gelato at Gelato di San Crispino (vegan flavours) and Fatamorgana (fully vegan).

On 30 May 2023 the user said they were planning a hiking trip in June 2023 and were deciding between the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP, and asked for a feature comparison of the two.
The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs 2 lbs 3 oz (990g), has a Gore-Tex membrane, a Vibram TC5+ outsole with 5mm lug depth, moderate ankle support, and costs around $130-$150.

The assistant stated the Keen Targhee II Mid WP weighs 2 lbs 1 oz (930g), has a Keen.Dry membrane, a Keen All-Terrain outsole with 4mm lug depth, a higher collar with more substantial ankle support, and costs around $140-$160.
On 30 May 2023 the user said ankle support was important to them because the mountain trails can be rough, and asked how the Keen.Dry membrane compares with the Gore-Tex membrane in the Merrell boot.

The assistant said Gore-Tex has a 28,000 mm water column rating against 10,000 mm for Keen.Dry, so Gore-Tex is more waterproof and durable, while Keen.Dry is more breathable and better suited to high-intensity activity or warmer weather.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they would go with the Keen Targhee II Mid WP because ankle support and breathability were most important to them, and asked how to care for the Keen.Dry membrane so it lasts.

The assistant advised caring for the Keen.Dry membrane by cleaning boots regularly with a soft-bristled brush, air drying them slowly away from heat, storing them in a cool dry place without folding, applying a waterproofing conditioner, and inspecting for delamination.
The user said they finally cleaned their white Adidas sneakers last month (April 2023), after meaning to for weeks, because they had got very dirty at an outdoor music festival.
The user cleaned the white Adidas sneakers by wiping the uppers with a mixture of soap and water, then air drying them on the balcony for a few hours, after which they looked like new again.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they had been wearing their new Vans Old Skool sneakers almost every day since getting them last weekend (the weekend of 27-28 May 2023), found them comfortable and easy to slip on and off, and planned to save the Adidas for special occasions or outdoor events.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they were planning a mountain trip in June 2023 and were choosing between the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP, and that their Converse Chuck Taylor All Star sneakers, owned for years, were perfect for an outdoor music festival attended last month (April 2023).

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs about 1.8 lbs, has a more substantial ankle collar and a more pronounced lug pattern, and has a snug fit, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP has a roomier toe box and is generally priced lower.
The assistant recommended the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof for the user's outdoor activities, while noting the Keen Targhee II Mid WP remained a good option for a roomier fit or a tighter budget.

The user said water had seeped into their Converse Chuck Taylor All Star sneakers at the music festival, especially at the heels where the soles were starting to wear down, and asked about the waterproofing of the two boots.

The assistant said both boots use a waterproof, breathable membrane (Merrell's M Select DRY and Keen's Keen.DRY), that no boot is completely waterproof, and that the user should apply a waterproofing treatment before the trip.
The user said they wanted the boots to keep their feet warm and dry in the mountains and asked about the insulation and warmth of the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof is rated for 20°F to 50°F (-7°C to 10°C) with a thermal insulation system, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP is rated for 15°F to 45°F (-9°C to 7°C) and uses Keen.Warm insulation.
The user said they were concerned about carrying extra weight and bulk on their feet, since their Converse Chuck Taylor All Star sneakers are very lightweight.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs approximately 1.8 pounds (816 grams) per pair and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP about 2.1 pounds (953 grams), with the Keen looking bulkier because of its wider toe box and taller ankle collar.
The user said they had been slipping on wet surfaces in their Converse sneakers, especially on the heels where the soles were wearing down, and asked about the traction and grip of the two boots.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof has a Vibram TC5+ outsole with 5mm lugs and a more pronounced heel brake, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP has a Keen.ALL-TERRAIN outsole with 4mm lugs and a more flexible forefoot.
The user said they were still deciding between the two boots and asked about breathability and moisture management, after their Converse sneakers got wet and stayed wet following the music festival.

The assistant said both boots have a breathable mesh lining, a breathable membrane that lets moisture escape while keeping water out, and a gusseted tongue that keeps debris and water out, and that both manage moisture far better than Converse sneakers.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they were choosing between the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP for an upcoming mountain trip, and that they had bought new black and white Vans Old Skool sneakers the weekend before (27-28 May 2023), which were very comfortable.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs approximately 2 lbs 1 oz (935g) per pair and has a snug fit with a roomy toe box, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP weighs approximately 1 lb 13 oz (820g), with a wider toe box and a more relaxed fit.

The assistant suggested the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof for a snugger fit and more aggressive tread, or the Keen Targhee II Mid WP for a more relaxed fit and a lighter, more agile feel, depending on the user's terrain and foot width.

The user said they would try on both pairs of boots, and that their Converse Chuck Taylor All Star sneakers, worn to an outdoor music festival last month, had soles starting to wear down on the heels, and asked if they should replace them soon.

The assistant said Converse soles should be considered for replacement if worn down to 1/8 inch (3 mm) or less, if the wear is uneven, if comfort or support has dropped, or if the shoes perform poorly in wet or slippery conditions, and that rotating shoes and applying sole protection can extend their life.

The user said they cleaned their white Adidas sneakers last month (April 2023) after weeks of meaning to, following an outdoor music festival they attended on the 15th. They were going to the mountains in a few weeks and asked how to waterproof their backpack and clothes.

The assistant recommended waterproofing the backpack with a lightweight waterproof backpack cover, a water-resistant treatment such as Nikwax Tech Wash or Granger's Performance Repel, and a seam sealer such as Seam Grip or Sil Net.
The assistant recommended packing a waterproof, breathable rain jacket and pants, storing clothes in waterproof bags or dry sacks, and checking the weather forecast before the trip.

The user said they bought a pair of black and white Vans Old Skool sneakers on a whim at the mall the weekend before (27-28 May 2023), had worn them almost every day since, and asked for waterproofing recommendations for their hiking boots.

The assistant recommended waterproofing the hiking boots with Nikwax Tech Wash or Sno-Seal, Scotchgard or Tectron, beeswax or Otter Wax, or Sil-Glyde or Sil-Net, after cleaning the boots first and applying the treatment evenly and sparingly.

The user said they planned to take their brown leather dress shoes to the cobbler for polishing and conditioning. They had worn the shoes to their cousin's wedding a few weeks before 30 May 2023, noticed signs of wear, and asked for maintenance tips.

The assistant's brown leather dress shoe care tips were to clean regularly with a soft dry cloth, condition and polish regularly, keep the shoes away from water, store them in a cool dry place using shoe trees, avoid bleach or ammonia, and consider waterproofing in humid or rainy areas.
The user said they had lent their spare pair of running shoes to their sister a few weeks before 30 May 2023, planned to take them to the track soon, and needed to remind their sister to return them.

The assistant gave general running shoe care tips: clean with a soft-bristled brush, store in a cool dry place away from sunlight, air dry without heat, rotate pairs, inspect for worn soles or loose stitching, and follow the manufacturer's guidelines.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they were planning a mountain trip next month (June 2023), had narrowed their hiking boots to the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof or the Keen Targhee II Mid WP, and needed to take their brown leather dress shoes to the cobbler.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof uses Gore-Tex and has a more substantial, sturdy ankle collar, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP uses Keen.Dry and has a more flexible ankle collar, so Merrell may suit users who prioritise ankle support.

The assistant said the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof is slightly heavier, tends to run narrower and has a slightly more rugged design, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP is more relaxed and comfort-focused.
On 30 May 2023 the user said they were leaning towards the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and asked for more information on the weight and fit differences between the two boots.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs 2 lbs 1 oz (935g) per pair and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP weighs 1 lb 13 oz (820g) per pair, both for men's size 9, a difference of about 4 oz (115g).

The assistant said the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof runs a bit narrower, has a slightly more spacious toe box and a snugger heel fit, and may need a slightly longer break-in, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP has more width and a more relaxed, comfort-focused fit.
The user said they would try on both boots before making a final decision and asked about the return and exchange policies for the boots.

The assistant stated Merrell offers a 30-day return window and Keen a 45-day return window, with exchanges handled by returning the item and placing a new order, refunds processed within 5-7 business days, and items required in original condition with tags and packaging.

The user said they would try on both boots at a local outdoor gear store on the weekend of 3-4 June 2023, and would take their brown leather dress shoes to the cobbler that Saturday (3 June 2023) to be polished and conditioned.

The user asked how to break in new hiking boots, and the assistant gave a break-in plan: days 1-2 wearing the boots around the house and walking on carpets, days 3-5 short 10-15 minute walks on flat surfaces with the hiking socks planned for the trip, and days 6-10 walks on uneven terrain while adding some weight.

The assistant advised checking new boots for pressure points and hotspots, testing them on varied terrain before the hike, and using blister prevention products such as moleskin or blister shields on high-friction areas.

On 30 May 2023 the user said they were deciding between the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof and the Keen Targhee II Mid WP hiking boots, and needed to remind their sister to return the spare running shoes lent to her a few weeks earlier.

The assistant stated the Merrell Moab 2 Mid Waterproof weighs 1.5 lbs against 1.7 lbs for the Keen Targhee II Mid WP and is comfortable right out of the box, while the Keen Targhee II Mid WP is generally priced lower and may need a slightly longer break-in period.
The user said they wanted to try both boots on to see which felt more comfortable, and asked whether there were any outdoor gear stores near them that carried both models.

The assistant suggested REI, Dick's Sporting Goods, Cabela's and local independent outdoor gear stores as places that may carry both models, and advised calling ahead to confirm stock and the user's size.
The user said they would check those stores and call to confirm stock, and also needed to get their brown leather dress shoes polished and conditioned, asking for good cobblers in their area.

The assistant said it could not recommend specific local cobblers without access to the user's location, and suggested searching 'cobblers near me', checking Google Reviews and Yelp, asking friends for word-of-mouth recommendations, and asking local shoe stores.

The user said they had lent their spare pair of running shoes to their sister because she wanted to start running, that she had said she would need them for only a week or two, and that it had now been almost a month.

The user asked for the best way to clean and maintain new hiking boots. The assistant recommended removing loose dirt, washing with mild soap such as Nikwax Tech Wash or Dr. Bronner's, air drying away from heat, applying Nikwax Waterproofing Wax or Sno-Seal, reapplying waterproofing every 2-3 months, and storing the boots with a boot tree.
On 1 July 2023 the user said they needed to restock BBQ sauce after using up their favourite Sweet Baby Ray's at a friend's place on Saturday 17 June 2023.

The assistant recommended BBQ sauce brands including Kansas City Masterpiece, Franklin Barbecue (a vinegar-based, slightly spicy sauce from Austin, Texas), Stubb's, Gates BBQ, Bone Suckin' Sauce, Dinosaur Bar-B-Que and Sweet and Smoky BBQ Sauce by Weber.
On 1 July 2023 the user said they had recently made Korean-style BBQ beef short ribs from an online recipe and asked for a good Korean-style BBQ marinade so they could try new flavours.

The assistant's basic Korean BBQ marinade used 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup gochujang, 2 cloves garlic (minced and sautéed), 1 inch grated ginger, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon crushed black pepper and optional 1/4 teaspoon Korean chili flakes, marinated for at least 2 hours or 8-12 hours overnight.

On 1 July 2023 the user said they had been experimenting with wood chips and had recently tried apple wood chips for the first time, which added a lovely fruity flavour to their grilled chicken, and asked for wood recommendations to pair with Korean-style BBQ.

The assistant recommended Korean Oak, Post Oak, Mesquite, Pecan and Cherry wood chips for Korean-style BBQ, advised soaking chips for at least 30 minutes, using 1/2 to 1 cup for a small to medium grill, and keeping smoker temperatures around 225°F to 250°F.

The user said they were thinking of hosting their own BBQ party and planned to invest in a new patio set for a large group, and asked for outdoor furniture that is durable, comfortable and easy to clean.

The assistant recommended Hanover Outdoor Furniture wicker sets, Polywood recycled plastic furniture including the South Beach 7-Piece Dining Set, Hampton Bay metal sets, the Winsome Wood outdoor sectional sofa and Flash Furniture outdoor bar stools.
The user said they planned a variety of BBQ dishes for the party, including vegetarian options for their non-meat-eating friends, and asked for easy vegetarian BBQ dishes that would impress guests.

The assistant recommended vegetarian BBQ dishes including grilled portobello mushroom burgers, roasted vegetable skewers, smoky grilled eggplant, BBQ jackfruit sandwiches, grilled vegetable quesadillas, stuffed bell peppers and grilled tofu satay.

The assistant also recommended vegetarian BBQ ribs made with jackfruit or mushrooms, a grilled vegetable wrap with hummus, and smoky grilled cauliflower served with tahini sauce, and advised labelling the dishes clearly so guests know what they can eat.
The user said they were thinking of serving Korean-style BBQ dishes such as bulgogi and galbi at the party and asked for vegetarian Korean-style BBQ options to serve alongside the meat dishes.

The assistant recommended vegetarian Korean-style BBQ options: deodeok bulgogi, grilled tofu bokkeum, vegetable skewers (yachae gohyang-yi), grilled portobello mushrooms (beoseot bulgogi), zucchini fritters (hobak jun), grilled eggplant (gaji bokkeum), vegetable japchae and Korean-style tofu tacos (dubu tacos).
